_source: Live Sound KB/Wiki/mic-library.md + CLAUDE.md mic shorthand (2026-06-16)
_note: ribbon=true forces NO 48V (flagged red in paperwork). phantom is the sane default; the wizard lets it be overridden per channel. 'aka' lists shorthand/alternates the matcher accepts. New mics added through the wizard are appended here and queued for the mic-library KB article.

mics.name: Earthworks DM6
mics.notes: SeisMic kick condenser, wide LF response. Body + sub. EQ differently from an attack mic and blend.

eq.character: SeisMic flat/extended-LF kick condenser. Honest, uncolored, huge sub reach — takes full shaping. Weakness: needs EQ to get a 'modern' kick, captures everything incl. bleed.

mics.name: Earthworks DM17
mics.notes: Rim-mount snare/tom condenser, fast and clear. Less low-mid build than a dynamic.

eq.character: Flat snare/tom condenser, fast, detailed, high SPL. Honest. Weakness: needs EQ for character.

mics.name: Earthworks SR20sp Gen 2
mics.notes: Matched overhead pair. Natural cymbal air; HPF for the genre.

eq.character: Flat, fast SDC, extended top, very accurate OH/room. Weakness: reveals harshness honestly, no hype.

mics.name: Earthworks SR25
mics.notes: Overheads or single kick condenser.

eq.character: Flat cardioid SDC, fast transients, natural top end for hat/OH. Weakness: uncolored — flatters nothing.

mics.name: Sennheiser MKH40
mics.notes: RF cardioid, extremely low noise. Flute, pipes, classical detail.

eq.character: RF cardioid condenser, near-flat with slight airy presence, very low noise. Pristine on flute/strings/detail. Weakness: clinical, proximity if close.

mics.name: Warm Audio WA-87
mics.notes: Brian's '87 JR' — his ONLY 87-family mic; there is no Neumann U87 in the kit. Any '87'/'U87' on Brian's paperwork = this WA-87. U87 clone, used on trombone at Memo.

eq.character: U87-style LDC clone, presence ~5-9kHz, smooth top, slightly more lower-mid than a real 87. Used on trombone. Weakness: proximity warmth, modest off-axis.

mics.name: Shure SM57
mics.notes: Snare/cab workhorse. Presence peak is at 6-7kHz (+5 to +7dB), not 3-5kHz — flat 200Hz-1kHz, only ~+2dB by 3kHz (Shure published curve, corrected 2026-07-26). Box/mud 300-500Hz on cabs, but the capsule dips slightly at 300-600 so cut lighter than reflex.

eq.character: Mid-forward workhorse, 40Hz-15kHz. Presence peak 6-7kHz (+5 to +7dB) — an upward ramp from ~2kHz, only ~+2dB by 3kHz, hard rolloff above 10k; -10dB at 40Hz. Proximity +6 to +10dB below 100Hz at 6mm. Small dip 300-600Hz. Weakness: thin lows, and that 6-7k peak stabs on bright transient sources.

mics.name: Shure SM58
mics.notes: Handheld vocal. HPF aggressively; cuts-only for feedback control.

eq.character: Cardioid vocal dynamic, presence ~4-6kHz, gentle low rolloff, proximity. Tough, consistent. Weakness: muddy if close, limited air, upper-mid spit.

mics.name: Shure Beta 58A
mics.notes: Supercardioid handheld; tighter rejection for loud stages.

eq.character: Supercardioid vocal dynamic, 50Hz-16kHz, <500Hz attenuated for proximity control, TWO presence peaks (~4kHz and ~10kHz) — brighter/more bite than SM58, tighter pattern, more gain-before-feedback. Weakness: those peaks can get strident/sibilant.

mics.name: Shure Beta 52A
mics.notes: Kick body/thump, inside. Blend with an attack mic.

eq.character: Tailored kick dynamic, scooped low-mids, presence lift ~4kHz, big lows. Click+thump voiced in.

mics.name: Shure Beta 91A
mics.notes: Boundary kick, attack/click layer on the head.

eq.character: Half-cardioid boundary kick/piano mic. Solid boundary low end + pronounced beater click; nominally flat (contour switch cuts 7dB@400 if engaged). Weakness: picks up shell boxiness ~300-500.

mics.name: Shure Beta 98H/C
mics.notes: Clip-on horn condenser.

eq.character: Clip-on cardioid condenser, 20Hz-20kHz, tailored/voiced presence for open natural horn/perc sound, tight pattern, gooseneck. Sax/brass/drum rim. Weakness: thin lows, the voiced presence can get edgy close.

mics.name: Shure SM81
mics.notes: Overheads, hat, acoustic instruments.

eq.character: Ruler-flat SDC, clean detailed highs with no harsh fizz, flat/6/18dB HPF. Accurate on hat/OH/acoustic — takes EQ well. Weakness: needs care on cymbal wash, no built-in flattery.

mics.name: Sennheiser MD 421-U (Silver Tail)
mics.notes: Brian owns the vintage 1970s MD 421-U 'Silver Tail' (native XLR, chrome connector base) — NOT the 2002 MD 421-II. Any '421' on Brian's paperwork = the 421-U. Same 421 element, so EQ character is unchanged. Toms, guitar cabs, brass. 5-position M-S roll-off on the body; no Tuchel adapter needed.

eq.character: Large-diaphragm dynamic, wide 30Hz-17kHz, extended low end + low-mid girth, voiced presence boost (~4-5kHz), 5-position bass rolloff (M=flat…S=-6dB<500Hz). Toms/brass/cabs. Weakness: low-mid bloat 200-400 if close.

mics.name: Sennheiser e609
mics.notes: Side-address cab mic, hangs over the grille. Tame 2-4kHz harshness.

eq.character: Flat-face cab dynamic, bright upper-mid/presence ~4-5kHz, supercardioid. Weakness: can be edgy ~2.5-4kHz on bright amps.

mics.name: Sennheiser e604
mics.notes: Clip-on tom dynamic, quick setup.

eq.character: Tom/snare clip dynamic, scooped low-mids, voiced attack. Convenient, fast. Weakness: thinner/boxier than a D-series, modest low end.

mics.name: Audix D6
mics.notes: Kick attack/click, scooped mids.

eq.character: Pre-scooped 'smiley' kick voicing: peaks ~63Hz and ~5kHz, deep mid scoop ~600Hz (-15dB). Thump+click baked in; needs almost no EQ. Weakness: one-trick, no midrange body.

mics.name: Audix i5
mics.notes: Snare, tight cardioid, punchy.

eq.character: Body lift ~+5dB@150Hz, presence ~+9dB@5.5kHz, mids slightly scooped vs SM57 — more open, more body. Weakness: that 5.5k peak can get harsh on a cracky snare.

mics.name: Audix D2
mics.notes: Small/mid toms.

eq.character: Rack-tom hypercardioid: +150Hz body, dip 500Hz-1kHz, subtle upper-mid lift. Punchy, articulate. Weakness: leaner deep lows than D4.

mics.name: Audix D4
mics.notes: Floor tom, more LF extension.

eq.character: Floor-tom/low source: flat to ~63Hz, rise ~80Hz, reaches 35Hz, smooth 800Hz-1kHz (not scooped). Deep, resonant. Weakness: less upper-mid attack — may need a touch of click.

mics.name: Audix M1280BHC
mics.notes: Ultra-compact hat condenser.

eq.character: Miniature hypercardioid condenser, extended 40Hz-20kHz, integrated preamp, RF-immune, tight isolation. Hi-hat/overhead/podium. Weakness: thin lows, upper-mid forwardness.

mics.name: Audix M1280B
mics.notes: Compact overhead condenser pair.

eq.character: Miniature cardioid condenser, 40Hz-20kHz, integrated preamp, RF-immune, generous front pickup. Overheads/cymbals/ensemble. Weakness: thin lows, room-sensitive.

mics.name: Audio-Technica Pro 35
mics.notes: Clip-on instrument condenser; sax/horn clip use.

eq.character: Clip-on cardioid condenser, 50Hz-15kHz (limited top), voiced presence lift, clamp mount. Drums/brass. Weakness: rolled-off extreme top, thin lows, plasticky upper-mid if close.

mics.name: Telefunken M80
mics.notes: Supercardioid handheld vocal, extended top.

eq.character: Handheld dynamic with hyped extended highs + air and scooped low-mids — condenser-like. Weakness: can over-sibilance, proximity buildup ~200-300.

mics.name: Shure Beta 56A
mics.notes: Tom/snare dynamic; confirm if used on vocal — earlier HF rolloff than a 58.

eq.character: Supercardioid dynamic, presence peak ~4-6kHz, tight pattern, good on snare/toms. Weakness: presence can get spiky, box ~400.

mics.name: Lauten LS-408
mics.notes: Side-address instrument condenser; snare/utility.

eq.character: FET large-diaphragm condenser voiced specifically for SNARE — pressure-gradient, ultra-high SPL/dynamic range, onboard HPF (80/140Hz) and LPF (5/12kHz) switches, tight rejection. Detailed, controlled crack. Weakness: snare-specialized, not a general vocal/room mic.

mics.name: Neumann KMS 105
mics.notes: Stage condenser vocal; more presence, more feedback-sensitive — cuts only.

eq.character: Supercardioid stage condenser. Flat 500Hz-7kHz, gentle air peak ~+5dB at 12kHz (voiced to add clarity without sibilance), internal always-on HPF -3dB@120Hz, partial proximity compensation. Smooth, airy, detailed. Weakness: feedback-sensitive, the 12k air can turn sibilant/harsh on a loud PA; proximity chest if eaten.

mics.name: Neumann TLM 102
mics.notes: Studio vocal/acoustic LDC.

eq.character: Compact LDC, presence/air boost ~+4dB above 6kHz peaking ~10-12kHz, fast. Bright, modern. Weakness: that HF lift can get sibilant on vocals/cymbals.

mics.name: AKG C414
mics.notes: Multi-pattern utility LDC.

eq.character: Versatile multipattern LDC, slight presence ~3-5k + air, detailed. Weakness: can be edgy/forward, needs taming on bright sources.

mics.name: AKG C422
mics.notes: Stereo LDC, two capsules one body — XY for horns, 2 console channels. Polarity-check L vs R.

eq.character: Vintage stereo LDC, two twin-diaphragm CK12 capsules (classic AKG brilliance rise ~6-12kHz), elastically suspended, M/S or XY. Smooth/full body with an airy top. XY on horns. Weakness: large/delicate, proximity, the CK12 top can get bright.

mics.name: Shure Beta 27
mics.notes: Side-address condenser; vocals/overheads/acoustic.

eq.character: Supercardioid LDC, flat 60Hz-3kHz, small peaks +2dB at 5.5k and 9k, -15dB pad, flatter than SM57. Open, clean cab/instrument mic. Weakness: slight 9k fizz on bright amps.

mics.name: Schoeps CMC6 + MK4
mics.notes: SDC cardioid; classical spot/overhead/soloist.

eq.character: Reference cardioid SDC, flat with a slight ~10kHz rise (compensates room HF loss), constant pattern, transparent/natural. Classical spot/main. Weakness: pricey/fragile, uncolored.

mics.name: Schoeps CMC6 + MK5
mics.notes: SDC switchable omni/cardioid; classical main pair / Decca tree.

eq.character: Switchable omni/cardioid SDC. BOTH patterns carry an HF lift vs the MK2/MK4 (brighter than the MK4); omni mode is natural with extended low end. Classical main pair. Weakness: that top lift can over-air a bright room — ease off presence/air.

mics.name: Schoeps CMC6 + MK41
mics.notes: SDC supercardioid; classical spot.

eq.character: Supercardioid SDC, tight, natural with gentle presence, great rejection. Classical spot. Weakness: slight off-axis coloration at extreme angles.

mics.name: DPA 4099 CORE+
mics.notes: Clip-on supercardioid for piano/strings/brass. Designed for the instrument — don't over-EQ. Don't touch the 10-12kHz boost.

eq.character: Clip-on supercardioid CORE+ condenser, ±2dB 80Hz-17kHz with a 2dB soft boost at 10-12kHz, very low distortion. Piano/strings/brass. Weakness: that HF lift is fixed (don't also boost air); proximity on loud sources.

mics.name: Countryman B3
mics.notes: Omni lavalier on strings; selectable HF caps +0/+4/+8dB. Light touch.

eq.character: Omni lavalier, selectable HF caps (+0/+4/+8dB), smooth, small. String/instrument clip. Weakness: omni = feedback/bleed risk, HF cap choice sets brightness.

mics.name: Line Audio OM1
mics.notes: Omni crowd/ambient, flown at Memo. Fixed EQ.

eq.character: Pressure (omni) condenser, very flat/natural, low self-noise. Flown ambient. Weakness: omni = lots of room/LF, needs HPF + mud cuts.

mics.name: Line Audio CM4
mics.notes: ORTF crowd pair, balcony at Memo. Fixed EQ.

eq.character: Cardioid SDC, flat/natural, ORTF room. Weakness: balcony distance = boomy LF + room mud, needs aggressive HPF.

mics.name: Deity S2
mics.notes: Short shotgun crowd pair, under PA at Memo. Fixed EQ.

eq.character: Deity S-Mic 2 supercardioid shotgun, 50Hz-20kHz, smooth/warm with NO presence-peak hype (unlike an MKH416), ~-18dB off-axis rejection, low coloration. Under-PA crowd mic at Memo. Weakness: rear (180°) rejection is only fair, so it does pick up PA HF — tame with the crowd-rig LPF.

mics.name: AEA R88
mics.notes: Stereo ribbon (Blumlein/MS). NO 48V — disengage phantom before patching. Passive — confirm preamp gain/impedance.

eq.character: Passive stereo ribbon (Blumlein/MS), 20Hz-20kHz with ribbon HF rolloff (~-10dB@18k), big smooth bass, never harsh. Classical room. NO 48V (passive — disengage phantom!). Weakness: dark top, low output, needs 60dB+ quiet gain.

mics.name: Royer R-121
mics.notes: Cab ribbon, blends under an SM57. NO 48V — destroys the ribbon. Sits 6-10dB below the 57.

eq.character: Figure-8 ribbon, flat 30Hz-15kHz, deep full (not boomy) low, defined mids, sweet natural top (never edgy/sibilant) rolling off above ~15k, proximity. Rear side records brighter. NO 48V. Weakness: soft top vs condensers, low output, proximity bloom.

mics.name: Royer R-10
mics.notes: Compact cab/room ribbon. NO 48V.

eq.character: Roadworthy passive ribbon: less throaty lows than the R-121, a touch brighter, smooth top, great on cabs/brass. Rear side brighter (offset ribbon). NO 48V. Weakness: still darker than condensers, proximity-prone.

mics.name: Radial J48
mics.notes: Active DI — keys, bass, acoustic, playback.

eq.character: Active phantom DI, clean/transparent, tight lows, high headroom. Bass DI. Weakness: clinical (no color).

mics.name: Neve RNDI
mics.notes: Active transformer DI — bass, guitar direct, synth.

eq.character: Active transformer DI, smooth musical top, gentle harmonic warmth, full lows. Bass/gtr/keys direct. Weakness: very slight HF softening vs a clean DI.

mics.name: Radial DI
mics.notes: Active DI — playback/utility.

eq.character: Clean DI, transparent. Weakness: depends on model; assume neutral.

mics.name: DI
mics.notes: Generic DI box. Confirm active/passive at load-in.

eq.character: Generic DI — neutral, full-range, no proximity. Treat tone at the instrument template.

mics.name: BSS AR 133
mics.notes: Added via ShowBuilder — confirm specs.

eq.character: Active DI, clean full-range with a slight high-mid air, solid lows. Acoustic/bass/keys. Weakness: minimal color — piezo quack passes through, treat at the instrument.

mics.name: Whirlwind IMP
mics.notes: Added via ShowBuilder — confirm specs.

eq.character: Passive DI, neutral/honest, reliable. Bass/keys direct. Weakness: passive = slight HF/level loss into low-Z, no active sparkle.

mics.name: XLR
mics.notes: Added via ShowBuilder — confirm specs.

eq.character: Unspecified source (placeholder). Confirm the actual mic/DI at the desk.

mics.name: Electro-Voice N/D 408
mics.notes: Vintage first-gen N/D 408 (no letter suffix), supercardioid. Rack toms, guitar cab, snare. Pivoting yoke — fits where a 421 won't. Bare "408" in paperwork means the Lauten LS-408, not this.

eq.character: Supercardioid N/DYM neodymium dynamic, 30Hz-22kHz close / 60Hz-22kHz far, brighter and more aggressive upper mids than an SM57, deliberate proximity lift, high SPL, tiny pivoting head. Toms/cabs/snare. Weakness: that upper-mid bite gets spiky on bright sources; close working distance piles low-mids; discontinued.
eq.research: web-verified 2026-07-26 (EV N/D 408B data sheet 531818-201; Gearspace / HomeRecording / Tape Op consensus)
